item.text: I’m reopening the current implementation and looking for the next layer of improvements: API clarity, internal duplication, and any remaining design debt after the first correctness pass.

I found the remaining design issue: probing logic is still split across multiple methods and deletion leaves tombstones unbounded, which means performance can quietly decay even though correctness is fixed. I’m consolidating probing into a single search result, adding tombstone-aware rehashing, and cleaning up the public surface with clearer primary methods plus compatibility wrappers.

items.text: Refactor the map around a single probe result and tombstone-aware rehashing
Add clearer primary operations while preserving existing method names as wrappers
Compile and run behavior checks for demo and deletion-heavy scenarios

item.text:
Further refactored [open_addressing_linear_probing.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/015_open_addressing_linear_probing/open_addressing_linear_probing.java) around a cleaner implementation model.

The main improvement is structural: the map now has a single probe path via `ProbeResult`, a nested `Entry` type instead of a separate top-level node class, clearer primary operations (`put`, `remove`, `size`, `containsKey`), and compatibility wrappers for the old method names. I also added tombstone tracking and same-capacity compaction, so deletion-heavy usage no longer accumulates probe debt indefinitely. `toString()` is now implemented for easier inspection, and resize/reinsert logic is isolated instead of routing through the public insert flow.

Verification passed with `javac open_addressing_linear_probing.java && java hashMap`, plus an additional stress check covering repeated deletes, reinserts, resizing, negative keys, and `containsKey`.
